scenario: [LCST.4.5.11] with [IRET.9.6]: a `Json` leaf of a kind with no row to the target is a TypeError, not an EngineError. `t`'s leaf is `true`, and [LCST.4.5.2] has no row from `Bool` to `Float`; `a`'s is the array `[1]`, which has none either. Each fact is matched by its own rule, so each fault has its own identity: a `TypeError` fact's identity is `(node, rule)` ([LERR.9.3]), and a fault raised while matching names the beta node as its rule ([LERR.9.11]), so two faults at one rule's node would be one fact. Each `d.body.c::Float?` raises a TypeError, which `handler` logs, and neither rule fires. A third fact, `f` with `2`, then converts and fires `from_number`, so the tier was not halted: an EngineError stops the pump where it is raised ([LERR.1.4.7]), and the step would return DS_ERR_ENGINE_HALTED, which fails the fixture ([RCTS.1.2.28]). Exactly ["type error", "type error", "converted f"]. PATH PINNED: `dsc.rete.lcst_4_5_11_dispatch`'s `is_bool` arm and its last arm, each `lcst_4_5_11_no_row`, a mismatch on a flagged node, in each runtime.
rules_ds:
schema Doc scope logical:
    k: String key
    body: Json mutable

rule from_bool:
    Doc d where d.k == "t" and d.body.c::Float? > 0.0
->
    log info "converted {d.k}"

rule from_array:
    Doc d where d.k == "a" and d.body.c::Float? > 0.0
->
    log info "converted {d.k}"

rule from_number:
    Doc d where d.k == "f" and d.body.c::Float? > 0.0
->
    log info "converted {d.k}"

rule handler:
    TypeError
->
    log info "type error"
